name: AA Badenhorst Kalmoesfontein
about: The flagship of the Badenhorst family. Old-vine Shiraz-led blend from dryland bush vines. Whole-bunch, natural yeast, aged in old oak foudres. Deep, savoury: blackberry, white pepper, fynbos, game.

name: AA Badenhorst Old Vine Chenin
about: From 40+ year-old dryland bush vines on the Paardeberg. Natural yeast, minimal SO2. Textured, complex: dried apricot, honey, herbs, wet wool. A natural-leaning Chenin that shows the old-vine potential of the Swartland.

name: AA Badenhorst Secateurs Red
about: Adi Badenhorst's everyday Swartland red — a Rhône-style blend from old dryland bush vines. Whole-cluster fermented with native yeasts. Juicy, peppery: red cherry, black pepper, herbes du Cap.

name: Abingdon Signature
about: From KwaZulu-Natal — one of the very few wine estates outside the Western Cape. The Sauvignon Blanc is grown at altitude in the Midlands, giving it a cool-climate character unlike any other SA wine: crisp, herbaceous, lime, and a nervy acidity. A rare and fascinating wine from SA's emerging cool-climate frontier.

name: Allee Bleue Magna Carta
about: From the historic 1694 estate. Magna Carta is a premium blend with dark fruit, spice, and structure. One of Franschhoek's most versatile estates.

name: Altima Chardonnay
about: From the high-altitude Swartberg farm. Cool conditions at 600m+ give this Chardonnay bright acidity and elegant citrus/stone fruit character unusual for Stellenbosch.

name: Altima Signature
about: From a high-altitude Swartberg farm in Stellenbosch. Cool-climate sourcing gives this unusual elegance for the region. Red fruit, herb, fine tannin.

name: Alto Rouge
about: From the historic Helderberg estate (land grant 1693). Alto Rouge is a classic red blend: cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, firm tannin. Old-school Stellenbosch at its best.

name: Asara Signature
about: From the boutique hotel estate near Stellenbosch. A crisp, herbaceous Sauvignon Blanc with nettle, gooseberry, and lime. Clean finish, good acidity. Well-priced for the quality.

name: Aslina Signature
about: Ntsiki Biyela's flagship Cabernet Sauvignon — she broke barriers as SA's first black female winemaker when she joined Stellekaya in 2004, then launched Aslina in 2016. Her Cabernet is structured and generous: cassis, dark chocolate, cedar, and a ripe tannin frame. A wine that carries the weight of South African wine transformation in every glass.

name: Ataraxia Chardonnay
about: From Kevin Grant's hilltop estate. Barrel-fermented, partial malo. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche. Bright acidity, elegant structure. Serene and precise.

name: Ataraxia Pinot Noir
about: From Kevin Grant's serene hilltop estate. Red cherry, forest floor, earth, florality. Light, elegant, fine-boned. A Pinot of great finesse.

name: Avondale Jonty's Ducks Chenin
about: From the organic/biodynamic estate on the Klein Drakenstein slopes. Jonty's Ducks Chenin is naturally fermented, textured, alive: apple, quince, honey, earth. The ducks that patrol the vineyards are part of the biodynamic ecosystem.

name: Avontuur Signature
about: From the estate equally famous for its thoroughbred horse stud and its red wines. Classic Stellenbosch Cabernet: cassis, cedar, eucalyptus, firm tannin. A solid, traditional estate red.

name: Backsberg Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the carbon-neutral Paarl estate. Cassis, cedar, mint, firm tannin. A solid, sustainably-produced Cabernet that shows environmental responsibility doesn't mean compromising on quality.

name: Backsberg Pinotage
about: From one of SA's first carbon-neutral wine estates. A fruit-forward Pinotage with plum, banana, chocolate and soft tannins. Sustainably produced and approachable.

name: Badsberg Signature
about: From the Breedekloof co-op in the Rawsonville valley. Fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc with apple, pineapple, and a crisp finish. One of the valley's most reliable value whites.

name: Bartinney Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the Jordaan family's steep Helshoogte Pass vineyards. Crisp, herbaceous, mineral: nettle, gooseberry, lime. The altitude and aspect give it a distinctive aromatic intensity.

name: Bartinney Signature
about: From a boutique family estate on the Helshoogte Pass. Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, and a polished structure. Small production, steep vineyards, meticulous farming.

name: Beau Constantia Syrah
about: From a modern estate with panoramic Cape Town views. Dark berry, white pepper, smoked meat, liquorice. A Syrah that benefits from the cool Constantia influence.

name: Bellevue Signature
about: A Pinotage specialist family estate in Stellenbosch. Ripe plum, banana, mocha, and integrated oak. Consistently rated among the best-value serious Pinotages in the Cape.

name: Bertha's Wines Signature
about: A small-producer Chenin Blanc with personality. Apple, quince, honey, and a crisp acid finish. Made in small batches with careful vineyard selection.

name: Beyerskloof Pinotage
about: From Beyers Truter, the winemaker who did more than anyone to champion Pinotage as a noble variety. Ripe plum, banana, mocha. Approachable and crowd-pleasing — the quintessential Pinotage ambassador.

name: Blaauwklippen Zinfandel
about: One of the very few Zinfandel plantings in South Africa, from this historic 1682 estate. Bramble, blackberry, black pepper, spice. A rare and interesting SA expression of this Californian-famous grape.

name: Boekenhoutskloof Semillon
about: From a single old vineyard in Franschhoek. Waxy, lanolin-textured: fig, lemon, hay, honey. Aged in old French oak. One of the most serious single-varietal Semillons in SA — a grape that Constantia made famous and Boekenhoutskloof has revived.

name: Boekenhoutskloof Syrah
about: The estate's flagship Syrah — sourced from a single Swartland vineyard. Whole-bunch fermented, aged in large French oak foudres. White pepper, blackberry, fynbos, smoked meat, and fine, chalky tannin. A serious, age-worthy Syrah that rivals the Northern Rhône.

name: Bon Courage Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the Robertson estate established in 1927. Their Cabernet Sauvignon is classic, structured: cassis, cedar, dark chocolate. Good value from a diverse, family-run estate.

name: Boplaas Cape Tawny
about: The benchmark SA port-style wine — aged oxidatively in old oak barrels for years. Tinta Barroca and Touriga Nacional from Calitzdorp. Caramel, walnut, dried fig, orange peel, toffee.

name: Boplaas Cape Vintage Reserve
about: The flagship fortified from SA's port capital. Made in declared-vintage years only, from old Portuguese varieties. Dense, powerful: black plum, dark chocolate, liquorice, spice. Will age 20-30+ years.

name: Boschendal 1685 Cabernet
about: Named for the estate's founding year. A classic Stellenbosch Cabernet at an accessible price. Blackcurrant, cedar, subtle oak, medium body. One of SA's best-value serious reds.

name: Boschendal MCC Brut
about: From the historic 1685 estate. Traditional-method Cap Classique from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Fine mousse, citrus, brioche, almond. A solid estate MCC from one of the Cape's most iconic properties.

name: Bouchard Finlayson Galpin Peak
about: Named after the Galpin Peak mountain. One of SA's most celebrated Pinot Noirs — single vineyard on Bokkeveld shale, planted 1989. Dark cherry, forest floor, truffle, fine-grained tannin.

name: Bouchard Finlayson Tinto
about: A red blend from the Hemel-en-Aarde estate. Shirah-led with Sangiovese and Nebbiolo. A unique SA take on an Italian-influenced style: cherry, herb, earth, leather.

name: Buitenverwachting Sauvignon Blanc
about: Beyond Expectations — from the cool Constantia slopes. Herbaceous and crisp: gooseberry, green pepper, lime. A benchmark Constantia Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Calitzdorp Wine Cellar Signature
about: From the co-op in SA's port capital. A Cape Tawny aged oxidatively: caramel, walnut, dried fig, orange peel, toffee. Serve slightly chilled with nuts or cheese — a Klein Karoo tradition.

name: Cavalli Signature
about: From the equine-themed estate with a celebrated restaurant. Dark fruit, cedar, mocha, and a polished structure. A modern Stellenbosch Cabernet that pairs well with their farm-to-table menu.

name: Cederberg Five Generations Cabernet
about: Named for the five Nieuwoudt generations who have farmed these 1000m+ mountain vineyards. Aged 18 months in new French oak. Intensely concentrated: blackcurrant, cedar, eucalyptus, dark chocolate, graphite.

name: Cederberg Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the highest vineyards in the Western Cape (1000m+). Extreme altitude gives intense flavour concentration and bracing natural acidity. Passion fruit, gooseberry, nettle, lime, flinty mineral edge.

name: Cederberg Shiraz
about: From the highest vineyards in the Western Cape (1000m+). The altitude gives this Syrah unusual elegance for SA: blackberry, white pepper, violet, herb. Fine tannin, bright acid. A unique high-altitude expression.

name: Chamonix Pinot Noir
about: From cool slopes in the Franschhoek valley. Their Pinot Noir is one of the few serious examples outside Walker Bay: red cherry, earth, mushroom, forest floor. High altitude gives it a distinctive finesse.

name: Charles Fox MCC
about: From Elgin's Cap Classique specialist. Traditional method, aged on lees. Fine mousse, citrus, brioche, almond. A serious MCC from SA's coolest wine region.

name: Clos Malverne Signature
about: The Auret blend from the Devon Valley estate. Shiraz-led with dark berry, white pepper, and a smoky edge. Approachable, food-friendly, and consistently good value.

name: Compagniesdrift Signature
about: A family estate with a distinctive barrel-shaped cellar. Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, and medium body. Solid, traditional Stellenbosch winemaking.

name: Constantia Glen Bordeaux Blend
about: A boutique Bordeaux-style blend from one of Constantia's smaller estates. Cabernet-led with Merlot. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate. Polished and age-worthy.

name: Craven Pinot Noir
about: From Mick Craven — minimal-intervention, sourced-fruit wines. His Pinot Noir is perfumed, light, and honest: red cherry, rose, white pepper. A new-wave Stellenbosch voice.

name: Creation Chardonnay
about: A Hemel-en-Aarde Chardonnay from the estate's high-altitude vineyards. Barrel-fermented, partial malolactic. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche, bright acid.

name: Creation Pinot Noir Reserve
about: From the high ridge of the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, JC Martin's Reserve Pinot Noir. Red cherry, forest floor, dried rose, mushroom, fine tannin. Aged 11 months in French oak.

name: Creation Syrah
about: From the Hemel-en-Aarde ridge. Cool-climate Syrah: blackberry, white pepper, violet, fynbos herb. More elegant than warm-climate Syrah — fine tannin, bright acid, and a savoury edge.

name: Crystallum Agnus Pinot Noir
about: The Bower family's flagship Pinot Noir from a single Hemel-en-Aarde vineyard. Red cherry, forest floor, truffle, dried rose. Fine-grained tannin, exceptional length. A collector's Pinot that rewards cellaring.

name: Crystallum Bona Fide Pinot Noir
about: From the Bower family. Sourced from several Hemel-en-Aarde vineyard sites. Red cherry, raspberry, earth, florality. A serious, age-worthy Pinot at a fair price.

name: Crystallum Paradisum Chardonnay
about: From the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley. Barrel-fermented Chardonnay with citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche. Elegant and precise.

name: Darling Cellars Signature
about: From the cool coastal Darling region near the West Coast. Sauvignon Blanc with nettle, gooseberry, lime, and a distinctive maritime freshness. The cooling Atlantic influence makes Darling one of SA's most interesting emerging white-wine regions.

name: Daschbosch Signature
about: An old-vine specialist in the Breedekloof. The Chenin Blanc is sourced from 30+ year-old dryland bush vines. Textured, mineral, honeyed — a serious wine that shows the Breedekloof's old-vine potential.

name: David & Nadia Elpidia
about: From David and Nadia Sadie (Eben Sadie's brother). Elpidia is their flagship Chenin from old Swartland bush vines. Natural yeast, minimal intervention. Honeyed, textured, complex: dried apricot, beeswax, fynbos.

name: De Grendel Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the Graaff family estate with sweeping Table Bay views. Tropical and herbaceous — passion fruit, guava, green pepper, lime. Bright acid, clean finish.

name: De Krans Cape Vintage Reserve
about: From SA's port capital, Calitzdorp. Touriga Nacional and Tinta Barroca, fortified and aged. Dense, dark: black plum, dark chocolate, liquorice. Will age 20+ years.

name: De Krans Chenin Blanc
about: A Platter 5-star Chenin Blanc from the Klein Karoo. Fresh, fruity, crisp: apple, pineapple, citrus. Remarkable quality from an arid region.

name: De Morgenzon Signature
about: The estate famous for playing Baroque music to its vines — and the wine seems to listen. Rich, barrel-fermented Chardonnay with citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, and brioche notes. Complex, textured, and consistently rated among SA's top Chardonnays.

name: De Wetshof Bateleur Chardonnay
about: The flagship barrel-fermented Chardonnay from Danie de Wet. Aged 9 months in French oak. Rich, complex: citrus, hazelnut, toasted almond, butter, and a distinctive limestone minerality from the Robertson soils.

name: De Wetshof Site of Origin Chardonnay
about: Danie de Wet's flagship Chardonnay — from a single limestone-rich vineyard in Robertson. Unwooded, fermented in stainless steel. Citrus, white peach, wet stone, chalky minerality.

name: Delaire Graff Botmaskop
about: From the luxury Helshoogte Pass estate. A Bordeaux-style blend with a Cape twist. Plum, dark berry, cedar, mocha. Polished, generous, and food-friendly.

name: Delaire Graff Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the luxury Helshoogte estate. Crisp, elegant: nettle, passion fruit, lime. A well-made Sauvignon from one of Stellenbosch's most visually stunning properties.

name: Delheim Vera Cruz Shiraz
about: The wine that put Delheim on the fine-wine map. From a single vineyard planted in 1972. Pepper, dark berry, smoked meat, earth. A Stellenbosch classic.

name: Diemersdal Sauvignon Blanc
about: From six generations of the De Waal family in Durbanville. Crisp, tropical, herbaceous. Passion fruit, guava, green pepper. Consistently reliable and well-priced.

name: Diemersfontein Carpe Diem Pinotage
about: The serious, traditional Pinotage — for purists. From old bush vines, aged in French oak. Plum, blackberry, earth, leather, integrated oak, structured tannin. A proper age-worthy Pinotage.

name: Diemersfontein Coffee Pinotage
about: The original coffee Pinotage — a style where specific oak staves impart coffee/chocolate notes, making Pinotage accessible to a mainstream audience. It became one of SA's most commercially successful Pinotage styles.

name: Diemersfontein Shiraz
about: From the Wellington estate famous for its Pinotage. Classic Shiraz: pepper, dark berry, smoked meat. A solid varietal expression from the foothills of the Hawequa mountains.

name: Dornier Cocoa Red
about: From the Swiss-owned estate with a contemporary art gallery. Cocoa Red is a Shiraz-led blend with dark fruit, mocha, and spice. Modern, polished, generous.

name: Drostdy-Hof Tulbagh Signature
about: A historic estate in the Tulbagh basin, surrounded by mountains. Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, and medium body. A solid, traditional Tulbagh red.

name: Duncan Savage Syrah
about: From sourced Swartland and Stellenbosch fruit, vinified with surgical precision. White pepper, blackberry, fynbos, smoke. Fine, almost crystalline tannin. A winemaker's winemaker.

name: Durbanville Hills Sauvignon Blanc
about: From cool maritime vineyards 20km from the Atlantic. Crisp nettle, gooseberry, passion fruit, lime. One of SA's best-value cool-climate Sauvignon Blancs.

name: Eagle's Nest Viognier
about: From steep, high-altitude Constantia vineyards. Apricot, orange blossom, peach, ginger. Low acidity, oily texture — a warm-climate white grown in a cool site, giving it unusual elegance.

name: Ernie Els Signature
about: From the golf legend's partnership with Jean Engelbrecht. The Signature is a premium Stellenbosch Cabernet/Bordeaux blend. Cassis, dark berry, cedar, mocha. Polished, generous, internationally acclaimed.

name: Fairview Goats Do Roam
about: The playful Rhône-style blend named after the famous goat tower. Approachable, fruit-forward: red berry, spice, soft tannin. One of SA's best-selling blended reds.

name: Fairview Pinotage
about: A modern, fruit-forward Paarl Pinotage. Red plum, banana, chocolate, soft tannin. Accessible and food-friendly.

name: Fairview Shiraz
about: Charles Back's Shiraz from Paarl granite soils. Black pepper, dark berry, white pepper, subtle oak. Consistently one of SA's best-value serious reds.

name: Flagstone Signature
about: A creative-label brand known for its literary back labels. The Dragon Tree is an approachable, fruit-forward blend: dark berry, spice, soft tannin. Crowd-pleasing and well-priced.

name: Flagstone Writer's Block Signature
about: Flagstone's creative-label Chenin Blanc range. Fresh, fruity, with apple and pineapple. A good-value, widely available Chenin for everyday drinking.

name: Franschhoek Cellar Cabernet
about: From the Franschhoek co-op. Good-value Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, medium body. Solid everyday drinking from the Huguenot valley.

name: Ghost Corner Sauvignon Blanc
about: From Dirk Human's brand, named after the Cape of Storms. Elim Sauvignon Blanc is intense, mineral, herbaceous. Nettle, green pepper, lime, flint. A wine from the edge of the continent.

name: Glen Carlou Chardonnay
about: From the Simonsberg-Paarl slopes. Barrel-fermented, aged in French oak. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, butter. One of the most consistently rated Chardonnays in SA at this price.

name: Glenelly Grand Vin
about: From the French-owned estate on the Simonsberg (May de Lencquesaing, former owner of Pichon Longueville). Grand Vin is a Bordeaux blend: cassis, cedar, graphite, fine tannin. Old-world elegance in the Cape.

name: Goudini Wines Signature
about: A Worcester valley co-op. Simple, fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc — a dependable everyday white at one of the lowest price points in SA wine.

name: Graham Beck Brut MCC
about: The flagship Cap Classique — Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, aged on lees for a minimum of 18 months. Fine mousse, citrus, green apple, brioche, almond. The wine that was served at both Mandela's inauguration and Obama's election night celebration.

name: Graham Beck Brut Rosé MCC
about: Méthode Cap Classique — South Africa's answer to Champagne, made the traditional way: bottle fermentation, hand-riddling, months on lees. Graham Beck's Robertson cellar sits on limestone soils that mirror Champagne's chalk. This Brut Rosé — Pinot Noir and Chardonnay — was famously poured at Nelson Mandela's 1994 inauguration and again at Barack Obama's 2008 election night.

name: Grande Provence Chardonnay
about: From the heritage Franschhoek estate with art gallery. Their Chardonnay is barrel-fermented, elegant: citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche. Polished and sophisticated.

name: Groenekloof Signature
about: From the Darling ward that has become a premium Sauvignon Blanc source. Crisp, herbaceous, and mineral: nettle, green pepper, lime, flint. The decomposed granite soils give a distinctive structure that separates Groenekloof Sauvignon from other SA regions.

name: Groot Constantia Gouverneurs Reserve Red
about: From SA's oldest estate (1685). The flagship red blend: Cabernet-led, aged in French oak. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, firm classic structure. A wine steeped in 340 years of history.

name: Groot Constantia Sauvignon Blanc
about: From SA's oldest estate (1685). Cool Constantia slopes give this crisp nettle, gooseberry, lime, and a flinty mineral finish. A historic estate's take on the Cape's great white grape.

name: Guardian Peak Signature
about: From the Lomo family's Shiraz-focused estate. Peppery, dark, structured: blackberry, white pepper, smoke. A consistently good-value serious Shiraz from the Helderberg foothills.

name: Hamilton Russell Chardonnay
about: The companion to their Pinot Noir — from the same cool, maritime Hemel-en-Aarde vineyards. Barrel-fermented, elegant: citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, and a bright acidity. One of SA's most consistently excellent Chardonnays.

name: Hamilton Russell Pinot Noir
about: In 1975, Tim Hamilton Russell made a bet that seemed reckless: that the cold, wind-battered, most-southerly tip of Africa could produce world-class Pinot Noir. Half a century later, his son Anthony has proved him right. Red cherry, forest floor, mushroom, dried rose, and a savoury minerality that speaks directly of the maritime site.

name: Hartenberg Chardonnay
about: From the family estate in the Bottelary Hills. Barrel-fermented, naturally evolved malolactic. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, butter. A benchmark Stellenbosch Chardonnay that consistently overdelivers for the price.

name: Hartenberg Rhine Riesling
about: One of the very few serious Rhine Rieslings in SA, from a cool south-facing block. Lime, green apple, jasmine, with a steely acidity. Off-dry style that ages magnificently for a decade or more.

name: Hartenberg Shiraz
about: Hartenberg's flagship red from their celebrated Shiraz vineyard on the Bottelary Hills. Aged 18 months in French oak. Black pepper, dark berry, smoked meat, white pepper. One of the most consistently rated Shiraz in Stellenbosch.

name: Haute Cabrière Pierre Jourdan Brut
about: From the estate with the best view in Franschhoek. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, traditional method. Fine mousse, citrus, brioche, almond. One of SA's most consistently excellent MCCs.

name: Haute Cabrière Pinot Noir
about: From the Franschhoek estate with the best view in the valley. Light, elegant, perfumed: red cherry, rose, earth. A food-friendly Pinot that pairs well with the estate's MCC.

name: Highgate Signature
about: From a KZN estate near Nottingham Road. A cool-climate Cabernet Sauvignon with red fruit, herb, and fine tannin — a completely different expression of the variety from what Stellenbosch produces. High altitude (1100m+) and summer rainfall make this one of the most unusual vineyard sites in the country.

name: Holden Manz Big G
about: From the boutique estate founded in 2010. Big G is a premium red blend: Cabernet, Merlot, Shiraz. Dark fruit, spice, mocha, vanilla. Modern and generous.

name: Iona Sauvignon Blanc
about: In 1997, Andrew Gunn bought a remote 420-hectare property in the Elgin valley, 420 metres up and within sight of the Atlantic. His bet — that this cold, slow-ripening, Kogelberg-biosphere site could produce Sauvignon Blanc of uncommon elegance — has become one of the defining stories of the Cape's cool-climate frontier. Nettle, passion fruit, green fig, lime zest and a flinty mineral edge.

name: Jordan Chardonnay
about: From Gary and Kathy Jordan's estate on the slopes of the Helderberg. Their Chardonnay is barrel-fermented with natural malolactic. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche. One of SA's most awarded Chardonnays.

name: Jordan Nine Yards Chenin Blanc
about: The Jordan family's flagship Chenin Blanc, named after their meticulous 'nine yards' approach to viticulture. Barrel-fermented, natural yeast. Rich, textural: dried apricot, honey, toasted almond, beeswax.

name: Kaapzicht Chenin Blanc
about: From the Steytler family's Bottelary Hills estate. Old bush vine Chenin: apple, quince, honey, wet stone. Consistently good value from a family that has been farming the same land since 1984.

name: Kaapzicht Shiraz
about: From the Bottelary Hills family estate (Steytler family since 1984). Their Shiraz is peppery, dark, structured: blackberry, white pepper, smoked meat. Consistently rated a top-value serious Shiraz.

name: Kanonkop Cabernet Sauvignon
about: Kanonkop's varietal Cabernet Sauvignon from the Simonsberg slopes. Structured, classic: cassis, eucalyptus, graphite, firm tannin. One of SA's most age-worthy single-varietal Cabernets.

name: Kanonkop Paul Sauer
about: The flagship Bordeaux blend from the estate that pioneered Pinotage. Cabernet Sauvignon-led with Merlot and Cabernet Franc, aged 2 years in French oak. Named after the patriarch who championed quality winemaking. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, and a tannic structure that demands a decade in the cellar.

name: Kanonkop Pinotage
about: The wine that proved Pinotage belongs among the world's noble reds. From the Sauer family's Simonsberg slopes — the same farm that pioneered the variety in 1925 — winemaker Abrie Beeslaar ferments in open concrete kuipe with punch-downs by foot. Black plum, banana skin, damp earth, and a structural tannin frame that rewards 10-15 years in the cellar.

name: Kanu Signature
about: An estate focused on Chenin Blanc and Sauvignon. The Chenin is fresh, fruity, and crisp: apple, pineapple, and citrus. A solid everyday-drinking Chenin at a fair price.

name: Ken Forrester Tatie
about: Named after Ken's mother Tatie, this is the accessible Chenin from the estate's range. Fresh, fruity, crisp: apple, pineapple, quince. A great introduction to the Forrester style of Chenin Blanc at an approachable price.

name: Ken Forrester The FMC
about: The wine that earned Ken Forrester his Mr Chenin Blanc title. Made in partnership with winemaker Martin Meinert from old, low-yielding bush vines on the 1689 Zandberg farm. Barrel-fermented with extended lees contact and aged in French oak. Dried apricot, honeycomb, toasted almond, beeswax and ripe pineapple — a glycerol texture that coats the palate, yet the natural acidity of old-vine Chenin keeps it from cloying.

name: Klein Constantia Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the cool Constantia slopes that once produced the world's most coveted wine. Crisp, herbaceous, mineral: nettle, gooseberry, lime, and a distinctive flinty edge from the decomposed granite soils.

name: Kleine Graniet Signature
about: A small Stellenbosch producer. Fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc with apple and citrus. Simple, honest, and well-priced.

name: Kleine Zalze Chenin Blanc
about: From the popular estate with golf course and restaurant. Their Chenin Blanc is fresh, fruity, approachable — apple, pineapple, crisp acid. One of SA's best-value Chenins.

name: Koelenhof Signature
about: A co-operative cellar producing reliable value wines. The Chenin Blanc is fresh, fruity, and crisp — a dependable everyday white at an accessible price point.

name: KWV Brandy Signature
about: From KWV's legendary brandy division — Cape pot-stilled brandy aged in French oak for a minimum of three years. Caramel, dried peach, walnut, spice, and a warm, spirity finish. KWV has been producing brandy since 1926, making it one of the oldest and most respected brandy houses in the Southern Hemisphere.

name: KWV Cathedral Cellar Cabernet
about: From the historic Paarl co-op founded in 1918. A structured Cabernet with cassis, cedar, dark chocolate. KWV's Cathedral Cellar range honours the estate's legendary barrel cellar.

name: L'Avenir Signature
about: A French-owned estate bringing Bordeaux precision to Stellenbosch. Their Pinotage is ripe, generous, and modern: plum, banana, mocha, and integrated oak. Consistently rated among the better Pinotages.

name: La Motte Pierneef Shiraz
about: From the Rupert family's Franschhoek estate. The Pierneef Shiraz is aged in French oak and shows classic pepper, dark berry, fynbos and smoked meat notes. Consistent and food-friendly.

name: La Motte Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the Rupert family estate. Crisp, fresh: nettle, gooseberry, lime. A well-made, dependable Franschhoek Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Laborie MCC
about: From the Paarl estate with a famous dining room. Their MCC is Pinot Noir + Chardonnay, traditional method. Fine mousse, citrus, brioche. A well-priced Cap Classique from a historic estate.

name: Lammershoek Old Vine Chenin Blanc
about: From old, dryland bush vines in the Swartland. Natural-yeast fermented, minimal intervention. Honeyed, textured, with dried apricot and a saline minerality. A wine for serious Chenin lovers.

name: Langeberg-Garcia Signature
about: A Klein Karoo co-op. Simple, fresh Chenin Blanc — a basic everyday white from one of SA's most arid wine regions.

name: Lanzerac Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the historic 1692 estate and hotel. Cassis, cedar, eucalyptus, dark chocolate. A polished, classic Stellenbosch Cabernet from one of the Cape's most luxurious properties.

name: Lanzerac Pinotage
about: From the historic 1692 estate and hotel. Their Pinotage is rich, ripe, and crowd-pleasing: plum, banana, mocha, chocolate. A quintessential Stellenbosch experience.

name: Le Chant Signature
about: A boutique estate with mountain views. Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, and firm tannin. Small production, careful winemaking.

name: Le Grand Domaine Signature
about: A luxury estate near Jonkershoek. Their Bordeaux blend is polished and structured: cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, and a firm tannic backbone. Elegant and age-worthy.

name: Le Riche Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the Le Riche family — Cabernet Sauvignon specialists. Old-vine Stellenbosch Cabernet, aged 24 months in French oak. Cassis, cedar, graphite, firm tannin. A classic in the truest sense.

name: Leeu Passant Old Vine Cinsault
about: From the Mullineux-Leeu partnership. Old-vine Cinsault sourced from a 1955 planting. Light, perfumed, elegant: red cherry, rose, white pepper. A serious expression of an underappreciated grape.

name: Lomond Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the estate near Gansbaai, on the Agulhas plain. Their Sauvignon Blanc is grown on single vineyard sites with different soils. Passion fruit, guava, mineral edge. One of the Cape South Coast's most interesting estates.

name: Lutzville Vineyards Signature
about: A West Coast co-op. Crisp Chenin Blanc with citrus and apple. The maritime influence of the Atlantic gives the wines a distinctive freshness uncommon in warmer SA regions.

name: Meerendal Heritage Pinotage
about: From the historic 1702 farm. A traditional Pinotage from old bush vines. Red plum, banana, earth, mocha. Heritage in a bottle.

name: Meerlust Cabernet Sauvignon
about: Meerlust's varietal Cabernet Sauvignon — from the same False Bay-influenced vineyards as Rubicon. Structured, firm, classic Stellenbosch Cab: cassis, eucalyptus, dark chocolate, and a tannin grip that rewards 5-10 years of patience.

name: Meerlust Merlot
about: Meerlust's varietal Merlot from False Bay-influenced vineyards. Plum, blackberry, chocolate, and soft, ripe tannin. A plush, approachable red that partners well with the estate's Cabernet in the Rubicon blend.

name: Meerlust Rubicon
about: The wine that defined SA Bordeaux blends. Named after the Rubicon river — Hanni Myburgh's father declared the estate had crossed the Rubicon when they first bottled it in 1980. A Cabernet-led blend with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot from the estate's False Bay-influenced vineyards. Cassis, cedar, graphite, dark plum, and a structured, age-worthy tannin frame.

name: Mont Rochelle Chardonnay
about: From the boutique estate (now a Virgin Limited Lodge). Their Chardonnay is barrel-fermented, rich, and generous: citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, butter. A wine with a view.

name: Montagu Cellars Signature
about: A Route 62 estate. Muscadel — sweet, grapey, floral, and simple. A Klein Karoo classic, best served chilled as an aperitif or with dessert.

name: Mullineux Old Vines Chenin Blanc
about: Andrea Mullineux's Chenin from old Swartland bush vines. Sourced from multiple parcels, naturally fermented, aged in old oak. Honeyed, textured, mineral: dried apricot, beeswax, wet stone, and a saline finish. Consistently rated among SA's top Chenins.

name: Mullineux Straw Wine
about: Chenin Blanc grapes air-dried on straw for 2-3 weeks, concentrating sugars and flavours. Rich, unctuous: dried apricot, honey, marmalade, caramel. Despite its sweetness, the natural acidity keeps it balanced. A modern SA classic that has few peers worldwide.

name: Mullineux Syrah
about: Andrea Mullineux was at the centre of the Swartland revolution from its first vintages — a Californian who came to study, stayed, and now makes some of the Cape's most precise reds. Her Syrah is sourced from a single parcel of dryland bush vines on decomposed-shale soils. Blackberry, white pepper, fynbos herb, a meaty savouriness and fine, almost chalky tannin. It unfolds for hours in the glass.

name: Muratie Amberley Cabernet
about: From one of SA's oldest estates (1685). Traditional, old-school Stellenbosch Cabernet: cassis, cedar, tobacco, eucalyptus. Firm tannin, built for ageing.

name: Musica de Sol Signature
about: A small Breedekloof producer. Fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc with apple and citrus. A pleasant, easy-drinking valley white.

name: Namaqua Wines Signature
about: From one of SA's largest co-ops, based in Vredendal on the West Coast. Fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc — simple, crisp, and one of the most widely available value whites in SA.

name: Nederburg Heritage Anchorman Chenin
about: From SA's most-awarded winery. Old-vine Chenin Blanc, barrel-fermented with natural yeast. Dried apricot, honeycomb, beeswax, and a rich, textural palate. Veritas Double Gold winner.

name: Nederburg II Heroes Cabernet
about: Part of Nederburg's premium II Heroes range, named after founder Johann Graue and his son. A structured, classic Paarl Cabernet: cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, firm tannin.

name: Neethlingshof Lord Neethling Pinotage
about: From the historic 1692 estate. A structured, traditional Pinotage with red fruit, banana, earth and integrated oak.

name: Newton Johnson Chardonnay
about: A Hemel-en-Aarde Chardonnay from high-altitude vineyards. Barrel-fermented, partial malolactic. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche, bright acid.

name: Newton Johnson Pinot Noir
about: From the family estate on the Hemel-en-Aarde ridge. Red cherry, forest floor, mushroom, dried rose. Fine tannin, elegant structure. One of the valley's most consistent Pinots.

name: Newton Johnson Syrah
about: From the Hemel-en-Aarde ridge. Cool-climate Syrah: blackberry, white pepper, fynbos herb, violet, and a fine, peppery tannin structure. More elegant than warm-climate Syrah — a wine that speaks of its cool maritime origin.

name: Nitida Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the boutique Durbanville estate. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, firm tannin. Small production, carefully managed — one of Durbanville's hidden gems for serious reds.

name: Nitida Sauvignon Blanc
about: From a boutique Durbanville estate. Crisp, herbaceous, passion fruit and nettle. Small-production, carefully made. One of Durbanville's hidden gems.

name: Nitida Titan Semillon
about: Nitida's flagship Semillon — full-bodied, waxy, with fig, lemon, hay and a lanolin texture. Aged in French oak. One of the few serious single-varietal Semillons in SA.

name: Nuy Winery Signature
about: From the co-op at the foot of the Langeberg mountains. Fresh Chenin Blanc with apple, pineapple, and a crisp finish. Good value from SA's largest wine-producing district by volume.

name: Oak Valley Chardonnay
about: From high-altitude Elgin vineyards. Barrel-fermented, citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut. Bright acidity, elegant structure.

name: Oak Valley Pinot Noir
about: From the 1898 estate in cool Elgin. Red cherry, raspberry, forest floor. One of the best-value serious Pinot Noirs in SA.

name: Overgaauw Cabernet Sauvignon
about: Four generations of the Van Velden family. Old-vine Cabernet with cassis, cedar, mint, and a firm tannic backbone. Consistently rated among SA's best-value serious Cabernets.

name: Overhex Signature
about: A Worcester estate with significant international distribution. The Sur Lie Chenin Blanc has a textured, leesy quality — more complex than typical Worcester whites. Lemon, apple, and a creamy mouthfeel.

name: Paul Cluver Chardonnay
about: From the cool Elgin plateau. Barrel-fermented, partial malolactic. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, brioche. Consistently rated a top-value serious Elgin Chardonnay.

name: Paul Cluver Pinot Noir
about: From the cool high-altitude Elgin plateau. One of the best-value serious Pinot Noirs in SA. Red cherry, raspberry, forest floor, earthy minerality.

name: Paul Cluver Riesling
about: One of the very few serious Rieslings produced in South Africa. From cool Elgin vineyards. Off-dry with bracing acidity: lime, green apple, white peach, jasmine. Ages beautifully for 10-15+ years.

name: Perdeberg Chenin Blanc
about: From the Paarl co-operative, specialists in dryland bush vine fruit. Their Chenin Blanc is fresh, fruity, crisp: apple, pineapple, citrus. One of SA's best-selling value Chenins.

name: Peter Falke Signature
about: From the German family estate by the Eerste River. An elegant Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, mint, and fine tannin. Precision winemaking in a stunning riverside setting.

name: Piekenierskloof Signature
about: From a high-altitude ward on the way to the West Coast. Old-vine Chenin Blanc with unusual intensity and a mineral edge. The altitude (500m+) and old vines give this a quality well above the Olifants River average.

name: Pink Valley Signature
about: A boutique Pinotage and Rosé producer. The Pinotage is ripe, fun, and approachable: plum, banana, chocolate. Doesn't take itself too seriously — and is all the better for it.

name: Porseleinberg Syrah
about: A single-vineyard Syrah from one of the most extreme sites in the Swartland. Planted on porphyritic (porselein) rock. Intensely concentrated: blackberry, white pepper, fynbos, crushed rock, game. A cult wine that sells out on allocation.

name: Precious Hidden Valley Signature
about: A small organic producer. Natural-yeast Chenin Blanc with apple, quince, honey, and a textural, slightly cloudy quality. Honest, alive, and interesting.

name: Raats Cabernet Franc
about: From the Raats family — the name synonymous with Cabernet Franc in SA. Their Cabernet Franc is sourced from old bush vines on the Simonsberg. Red berry, herb, graphite, violet, fine tannin. One of the world's best-value serious Cabernet Francs.

name: Raats MR de Compostella
about: The flagship Bordeaux-style blend — Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Malbec. Each varietal vinified separately and aged in French oak. Cassis, graphite, dark chocolate, violet. Consistently ranked among SA's top 10 reds.

name: Rall Chenin Blanc
about: From Mariana Rall, sourcing old-vine fruit from the Swartland. Her Chenin Blanc is textured, mineral, serious: dried apricot, honey, wet stone, saline. Small production, high demand.

name: Remhoogte Bush Vine Chenin
about: Family-run estate on the Bottelary Hills. Their bush vine Chenin is old-vine, hand-harvested, naturally fermented. Apple, quince, honey, wet stone. Textured and serious.

name: Remsberg Signature
about: A historic family estate Cabernet. Cassis, cedar, medium body, and a traditional Stellenbosch character. Solid and dependable.

name: Reyneke Cabernet Sauvignon
about: Stellenbosch's leading biodynamic estate. Their Cabernet Sauvignon is grown without synthetic inputs, fermented with native yeasts. Cassis, herb, earth, fine tannin. Pure and alive.

name: Robertson Winery Chenin Blanc
about: From the Breede River Valley co-op. Fresh, fruity Chenin with apple, pineapple, and a crisp finish. One of SA's best-selling value whites.

name: Ruitersbosch Signature
about: A small Tulbagh producer. Fresh, fruity Chenin Blanc with apple and citrus. Honest, simple, and well-priced.

name: Rustenberg Chardonnay
about: A Stellenbosch Chardonnay benchmark. Barrel-fermented with natural malolactic, aged 9 months in French oak. Citrus, stone fruit, hazelnut, butter — well-integrated oak, bright acid. Consistently rated among SA's top Chardonnays at this price point.

name: Rustenberg John X Merriman
about: Named after the pioneer who modernised the estate in the 1940s. A Bordeaux-style blend of Cabernet and Merlot. Cassis, plum, cedar, herb. Medium-bodied, approachable — the more accessible sibling to the flagship Peter Barlow.

name: Rustenberg Peter Barlow Cabernet
about: Named after Peter Barlow, who bought Rustenberg in 1941 and restored it. This single-vineyard Cabernet from the estate's oldest block (planted 1948) is one of SA's longest-lived reds. Cassis, cedar, tobacco, eucalyptus.

name: Sadie Columella
about: The wine that announced Eben Sadie — and the Swartland — to the world. Named for Lucius Columella, the Roman agricultural writer, this Rhône-influenced blend is sourced from ancient dryland bush vines on the decomposed granite of the Paardeberg. Profound depth: blackberry, white pepper, fynbos herb, crushed rock, and cured meat, wrapped in fine-grained tannin.

name: Sadie Palladius
about: Eben Sadie's flagship white — a blend of up to 11 varieties (including Chenin Blanc, Grenache Blanc, Clairette, Viognier) sourced from old vineyards across the Swartland and Citrusdal. Complex, textured, profound: dried apricot, honey, herbs, fynbos, wet stone. A wine that redefines what a SA white can be.

name: Sadie Skurfberg
about: From a windswept, iron-rich hilltop in the Citrusdal Mountain ward — vines planted in 1962, surviving without irrigation in one of the harshest old-vine sites in the Cape. Eben Sadie considers these dryland bush vines a national treasure. Salted honey, dried apricot, beeswax, wet stone, and a finish that seems to last for minutes.

name: Saronsberg Signature
about: A premium estate in the Tulbagh valley. The Shiraz is pepper-driven, dark, and structured: blackberry, smoked meat, spice, and a firm tannic backbone. One of the best wines from this emerging region.

name: Simonsig Kaapse Vonkel Brut
about: The original SA Cap Classique — first produced in 1971 by Frans Malan, predating every other MCC. Pinot Noir + Chardonnay, traditional method. Fine mousse, green apple, brioche, almond.

name: Simonsig Pinotage
about: Simonsig's Pinotage from the Simonsberg slopes. Ripe plum, banana, mocha, and integrated oak. Good value introduction to the variety from a pioneer estate.

name: Skilpadvlei Signature
about: A family estate producing broad-range value wines. The Pinotage is ripe, fruity, and approachable: plum, banana, mocha. One of SA's best-value Pinotages.

name: Slanghoek Signature
about: A family-run co-op in the Slanghoek valley. Fresh, fruity, crisp Chenin Blanc. Simple, honest, and well-priced for everyday drinking.

name: South Hill Pinot Noir
about: From a small Elgin producer. Their Pinot Noir is light, perfumed, elegant: red cherry, raspberry, earth. Cool-climate purity from the Kogelberg Biosphere.

name: Spier Creative Block 5
about: A five-varietal Bordeaux-meets-Rhône blend from Spier. Each year the winemaker selects the best 5 barrels. Ripe, generous: black plum, cassis, spice, vanilla.

name: Springfield Life from Stone
about: From a single vineyard of quartz-stone soils in Robertson. Wild-yeast fermented, unfiltered, unfined. Intense minerality, gunflint, green fig, white peach. A wine with a cult following.

name: Springfield Wild Yeast Sauvignon Blanc
about: Naturally fermented with wild yeast from the vineyard, giving it a distinctive textural quality and complex aromatic profile. Passion fruit, guava, green fig, and a subtle reductive note that Springfield fans adore.

name: Steenberg MCC Brut
about: From the oldest farm in Constantia (1682). Traditional method, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Fine mousse, citrus, brioche, almond. A sophisticated Cap Classique from one of the Cape's most historic properties.

name: Steenberg Sauvignon Blanc
about: From the oldest farm in Constantia (1682). Cool maritime conditions give crisp nettle, gooseberry, lime and a mineral finish. Consistently rated among Constantia's best.

name: Stellenbosch Reserve Signature
about: A cooperative brand Cabernet Sauvignon. Cassis, cedar, medium body. A reliable, well-priced Stellenbosch red for everyday drinking.

name: Stellenzicht Pinotage
about: From the revived historic estate. Ripe plum, banana, mocha. A solid, approachable Stellenbosch Pinotage.

name: Stellenzicht Signature
about: From a historic estate revived under new ownership. The Shiraz is peppery, dark, and structured: blackberry, white pepper, smoke. A welcome return for a Stellenbosch name with heritage.

name: Strandveld First Sighting Sauvignon
about: From Africa's southernmost vineyards, windswept and intense. First Sighting Sauvignon Blanc is crisp, herbaceous, concentrated: nettle, passion fruit, lime, sea salt. A wine shaped by the wind.

name: Testalonga El Bandito Chenin
about: Craig Hawkins' cult natural Chenin. Skin-contact, wild yeast, no added sulphur. Orange wine style: dried apricot, honey, tannic grip, oxidative notes. Polarising and fascinating.

name: The Chocolate Block
about: The blend that opened the door for premium South African wine on the world stage. When Marc Kent first assembled it in 2000, Rhône-style blends were rare in the Cape; today it is one of the most recognised SA wine names globally. Syrah-led with Grenache, Cinsaut and Mourvèdre — dark plum, white pepper, smoked meat, liquorice and a characteristic dark-chocolate undertone.

name: Thelema Sauvignon Blanc
about: Thelema's flagship white — from the Helshoogte Pass vineyards. Crisp, herbaceous, gooseberry and nettle with a mineral finish. One of the best-value serious Sauvignon Blancs from Stellenbosch.

name: Tokara Director's Reserve Red
about: The flagship Bordeaux-style blend from the modern Helshoogte Pass estate. Cabernet-led with Merlot and Petit Verdot. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate, graphite. Aged 18 months in French oak.

name: Tokara Director's Reserve Red
about: From the modern estate on the Helshoogte Pass. The Director's Reserve is a Cabernet-led Bordeaux blend from the estate's best vineyards. Cassis, cedar, dark chocolate. Polished and age-worthy.

name: Van Loveren Christina
about: One of SA's most popular value reds — a blend named after the Retief family matriarch. Ripe berry, spice, soft tannin. Crowd-pleasing and accessible.

name: Van Loveren Merlot
about: From the popular Robertson family estate. Plum, blackberry, chocolate, soft tannin. An approachable, food-friendly red for everyday drinking.

name: Vergelegen Cabernet Sauvignon
about: From the estate's Helderberg vineyards. Classic Stellenbosch Cabernet: cassis, cedar, eucalyptus, dark chocolate. Firm, ripe tannin. A more approachable sibling to the flagship GVB.

name: Vergelegen GVB Red
about: From one of South Africa's most historic estates — founded in 1700 by Governor Willem van der Stel, restored by Anglo American in 1987. The GVB Red is the flagship Bordeaux-style blend, Cabernet-led with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot, grown on the estate's Helderberg-amphitheatre vineyards. Cassis, cedar pencil, graphite, dark chocolate and firm, ripe tannin. Built for the long haul.

name: Vergelegen Sauvignon Blanc
about: From cool vineyards on the Helderberg. Crisp, herbaceous: nettle, gooseberry, passion fruit, lime. A benchmark Stellenbosch Sauvignon Blanc at a fair price.

name: Vilafonté Series C
about: The Cabernet-dominated sibling to Series M. Structured, age-worthy, with intense cassis, graphite, dark chocolate, and a firm,classic tannic backbone. One of SA's most internationally acclaimed reds.

name: Vilafonte Series M
about: From the partnership between Zelma Long, Phil Freese and Mike Ratcliffe. Series M (Merlot-dominated) is one of SA's most expensive and sought-after reds. Plum, dark chocolate, mocha, cedar. Profoundly structured.

name: Vin de Constance
about: A resurrected legend. When Simon van der Stel planted Constantia in 1685, he could not have known his Muscat-based natural sweet wine would become the most coveted in 19th-century Europe — requested by Napoleon on his deathbed, written of by Dickens and Jane Austen. After phylloxera killed the vines, the wine vanished for a century. In the 1980s, Klein Constantia traced the original clones, replanted the steep sea-facing slopes, and painstakingly recreated it. Orange marmalade, apricot, honey and linden blossom — luscious yet poised.

name: Visio Vintners Signature
about: A boutique Devon Valley estate. Cabernet Sauvignon with cassis, cedar, and dark chocolate. Small production, careful vineyard management.

name: Vondeling Monsonia
about: From the Voor-Paardeberg — an emerging terroir on decomposed granite. A Rhône-style blend: Shiraz, Mourvèdre, Grenache. Pepper, dark berry, herbes du Cap, liquorice.

name: Warwick Pinotage
about: From the estate pioneered by Norma Ratcliffe. Ripe plum, banana, mocha, and integrated oak. A well-made varietal Pinotage from the estate that helped put the variety on the map.

name: Warwick Three Cape Ladies
about: A Cape Blend — Pinotage, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Merlot. Pioneered by Norma Ratcliffe (The First Lady of SA Wine). Ripe berry, spice, mocha, soft tannin.

name: Waterford Estate Jem
about: Waterford Estate's flagship — a blend of up to 9 varietals, named after the late Jem Montgomery. Dark fruit, spice, cocoa, lavender. One of Stellenbosch's most popular premium blends.

name: Winshaw Signature
about: A family estate producing a broad range. The Cabernet Sauvignon has cassis, cedar, and soft tannin. Approachable and good value.

name: Yonder Hill Signature
about: A family estate with restaurant and accommodation. The Merlot is generous and soft: plum, blackberry, chocolate. A comfortable, crowd-pleasing Stellenbosch red.

name: Zandvliet Shiraz
about: From the Robertson estate on limestone soils. Their Shiraz is peppery, dark, structured: blackberry, white pepper, liquorice. Limestone gives it a distinctive minerality.

name: Zorgvliet Signature
about: A historic Banghoek estate with a renowned restaurant. The Cabernet Sauvignon has cassis, cedar, and eucalyptus — classic cool-valley Stellenbosch character.

name: Zorgvliet Silver Mist Blanc
about: From the Banghoek Valley estate. A fresh, aromatic white blend: citrus, apple, blossom. Named after the morning mist that settles in the valley.
